scope: Static CSDL 4.01 XML/JSON authoring and tolerant consumption; source paragraphs are in conformance-requirements.json. Prefix matching uses the longest section prefix.

status_meaning.covered: Direct implementation and regression evidence for this paragraph; not a blanket certification of its enclosing section.
status_meaning.partial: Implementation and tests exist, but known behavior or direct positive/negative evidence remains incomplete.
status_meaning.unsupported: A known static obligation is not implemented completely.
status_meaning.advisory: SHOULD guidance deliberately does not reject otherwise valid documents.
status_meaning.outside-static-scope: Transport, runtime data, execution, or specification metarule; no static validator assertion is appropriate.

groups.note: RFC requirement-word interpretation; not an executable CSDL constraint.
HTTP content negotiation belongs to the hosting service. JSON media-type output options are implemented separately from HTTP negotiation.
Prose takes precedence over schemas; the audit includes semantic checks beyond document shape.
Member, parameter, and expression order retained. The syntactic model groups structural/navigation members and container children by kind, so it cannot reproduce all interleaving.
Names and scope identity checked. Case-only differences remain advisory; programmatic models need the source checks supplied by guarded serialization.
Term identity plus qualifier plus resolved target identify duplicate applications.

Document grammar, service intent, includes, loader cache, cycles and alias scope implemented. Reference and Include annotations are retained and resolved. DocumentLoader::inspect_reference exposes Core.SchemaVersion before retrieval, including cache hits; strict JSON alias-only spelling is enforced.
Schema, alias and annotation group validation implemented. Strict JSON parsing enforces alias-only references; tolerant resolution accepts both spellings.
Static identity/inheritance rules covered by both-format tests; data-instance obligations are runtime responsibilities.
Key paths, types, aliases and related-entity key coverage checked. Actual key uniqueness and language-independent URLs are outside the static model.

Names, types, facets, defaults and version differences checked. Imported primitive ABNF cases execute in XML and JSON; unrepresentable unknown collection-nullability conversion is rejected. Exhaustive facet evidence remains partial.
Partners, constraints, containment, cardinality and delete declarations are checked; row values, relationship integrity and executing delete actions are outside static validation.
Complex inheritance and declaration rules implemented; case-only names advisory, dynamic instance properties outside scope.
Enum declarations and implicit XML values checked. JSON annotation numeric enum values and all flag combinations need further expression tests.
Underlying types and inherited facets checked; expand direct XML/JSON cases for every abstract type use.

Overloads, binding and return types checked. Authored-versus-defaulted nullability is preserved for JSON collection signatures. Cross-version parameter order and function side effects require a service/history context.
Container identity, inheritance and unique child names checked. Service-data and queryability recommendations belong to the host.

Resolved binding graph semantics checked. JSON same-container target spelling is validated and normalized during options output; recursive-path variants need more clause evidence. Missing bindings remain advisory.
Import overload identity, unbound requirement, target entity-set identity and return compatibility checked; not every clause yet has an independent paired-format case.
See action imports; function imports retain unbound overload candidates.

Semantic diagnostics remain nonfatal for tolerant consumers. Profile parsing recovers invalid/unavailable annotation expressions with optional ParseReport diagnostics. Legacy APIs preserve their error behavior.
Term/default/base-term/applicability checks implemented; per-member record completion from base-term applications is implemented.
Targets and term casts use resolved graph nodes. Document scope checks include structural and annotation paths; exhaustive clause evidence remains partial.

Common lexical forms/ranges/facets tested. The official ABNF corpus is imported and classified; 66 primitive/identifier cases execute with explicit representation adaptation. Arbitrary decimal text, numeric enums and source-format literal typing are implemented; complete clause evidence remains partial.
Operators, metadata, casts and records implemented with recursive checks. See more specific path/function/record limitations.

Typed key/index selectors, counts, empty paths, collection multiplicity, media terms, navigation annotation suffixes, and target-relative contexts are implemented. Literal domains and exhaustive clause-level evidence remain partial.

Declared functions and common canonical functions checked. Full canonical overload catalog, numeric promotion, geography functions, custom client-function registries and URI-template map typing remain incomplete.
Arity, Boolean condition, branch compatibility and collection-only omitted else checked; execution is outside scope.
Labels bind by canonical schema name, cycles and duplicates are diagnostic. Add all cross-document visibility and nested-expression annotation cases.
See labeled elements; unresolved names are explicit diagnostics.
Record members, abstract types, duplicates and required values checked. Base-term member inheritance and typed open records require additional checks.
URL operand is checked as String. Returned resource representation needs caller-supplied type/evaluation context; no HTTP fetch occurs.
Version guards and consumption/authoring profiles are explicit. The remaining partial/unsupported rows preclude a full service or client conformance claim.

overrides.note: Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove combined structural/navigation member uniqueness and declaring-type name prohibition, including permitted inherited/base-name cases and prohibited narrowing redeclarations.
Independent source fixtures cover required members, every enum integer boundary, flags, implicit XML value order, primitive-only definitions and re-specification prohibition for each inherited facet.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove entity target kinds/scope, collection Nullable prohibition, complex-owner Partner prohibition, partner reciprocity and all referential nullability combinations.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover decimal versus temporal precision bounds, scale/precision ordering and case-insensitive floating scale version guards. Variable scale casing is accepted and output normalized to lowercase.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover declared/inherited keys for sets and containment collections, complete related keys including navigation on complex values, and alias identifier/uniqueness rules across inherited structural/navigation properties.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures exercise key scalar types, nullability, collection rejection, enum/type-definition keys, nested complex paths and direct-property alias prohibition. Related-entity and inherited alias obligations have separate focused evidence.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove inheritance cycle checks, open/media/abstract inheritance restrictions and version-specific declared/inherited key requirements.

Independent source fixtures cover schema type-name uniqueness, reserved namespaces, alias identifiers and XML schema/external annotation-group required members. Mixed global-namespace and cross-document obligations remain partial.
Independent XML and JSON positive/negative source fixtures cover required reference/include members, array/object shape, filters and document-global included namespace uniqueness.
Normative wording occurs inside an illustrative vocabulary annotation, not a CSDL authoring rule.
Explicit IEEE754Compatible and metadata options, arbitrary precision decimals and loader-backed graph validation are implemented. Exhaustive clause evidence remains open.
Default/control-field omission is a size optimization, not a reason to reject a semantically valid model.
Strict source parsing rejects namespace-qualified references where an alias exists and qualified same-container binding targets; tolerant parsing accepts them.
Case-only names, unknown future AppliesTo values, explicit 4.0 collection nullability, queryability and binding coverage do not make strict validity fail; no dedicated warning stream yet.
Obligation concerns runtime entity values, URLs, payloads, or execution rather than static metadata.
Reference annotations and Core.SchemaVersion inspection hooks are implemented. Retrieval query policy belongs to the caller; exhaustive clause evidence remains partial.
Ordered indexes bind to typed selected-item nodes. Runtime index evaluation is outside static scope; full clause evidence remains partial.
Strict grammar regression tests cover missing/multiple document wrappers and required version/schema structure.
Document-global alias collision/reserved-name tests run before normalization.
Positive collection-item and negative scalar two-operand If cases are in conformance_audit.rs.
Absent authored defaults and length facets stay absent; consumer code must not invent a service constraint.
